tools.name: search_events
tools.description: Start here for discovery: search FrontRowTickets.com ticket inventory by free text, city, date range, and category (sports, concerts, theater, comedy). All filters are optional and combine freely; returns up to 'limit' events (default 10, max 50, no further pages), soonest first, with ticket counts

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: Full details for one event: venue, date, ticket count, price range, and sections. The record is live-refreshed from the catalog when called (cached copy otherwise), so this is the fullest picture of the event. Prefer get_availability when the only question is 'can I get N tickets at or under $X' — i

tools.name: get_availability
tools.description: Answers 'can I get tickets for this event?' for one event: refreshed from the live source at call time, returning current availability and starting price. max_price is a hard gate — the event is reported only if its starting price is at or below it (otherwise availability:null with a note); quantity

tools.name: get_deals
tools.description: Use when budget is the primary filter: returns the cheapest available events under a required max_price cap (applied to each event's starting price), cheapest first, up to 25 results; events without pricing data are excluded. City and date range are optional additional filters. Use search_events for

description: Return actual seat listings for one event — section, row, quantity, seat range, base and all-in price per ticket, listing notes, and fee detail — cheapest all-in first. Use after search_events when the user wants seat options to choose from, not just a starting price. max_price caps the ALL-IN price

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_seat_options" stacks urgency/override words (important, always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
